analysis:
This PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md, with no code or control change visible. I found no concrete security regression. The head text ends at line 502, and the base excerpt starts at 503, so I could not diff the two. The head's SSD prefix-cache table (lines 495-502) matches T-041's documented posture: 30-minute TTL maximum, a disk budget defaulting to half the available space, the 20 GiB write reserve, and the ephemeral/test-root settings accepted only with ALLOW_EPHEMERAL. The base lines 503-509 (TEST_PERSISTENT_KEY, TTL <=1800, daily write budget, strict fsync) could not be matched against the head. The head adds or documents the following, all as docs only:
- The worker qualification opt-in DARKBLOOM_APP_ATTEST_WORKER_QUALIFICATION (lines 127-143). It is forwarded to launchd, uses exact `1`, and creates no local trust (TB-011, T-052, T-053).
- Endpoint-resumption and logout semantics (lines 67-88): logout uses issuer metadata bound to the saved token, and missing metadata means local-only logout with a warning (A-008).
- Forwarded MiMo env controls, including COMPLETE_PREFIX cache enablement (lines 337-345, T-041).
- A documented auth-token path override, DARKBLOOM_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH (line 283, A-008).
A next pass should check the real source behind these claims, for example the LaunchAgent passthrough allow-list in `LaunchAgent.swift` and the auth-token loading in `DeviceAuth.swift`. The documentation alone does not show whether the code matches.
